recreation_brief:
1. Set the slide background to plain white (#FFFFFF).
2. Draw the header band: a light-gray (#E8E8E8) rectangle spanning the full slide width, from the top edge down to about 15% of slide height, with no border.
3. Center the title 'K -Nearest Neighbors Algorithm' in the header band in large bold sans-serif, split-colored: 'K -Nearest Neighbors' in red (#CC0000) and 'Algorithm' in blue (#0000CC).
4. Place a yellow (#F5E97A) circle badge in the top-right corner of the header band containing the number '41' in dark (#333333) text.
5. Draw the content box: a large rectangle with a thin red/maroon (#B03030) border and no fill (the white background shows through), spanning the full width with side margins and from about 15% to 100% of slide height.
6. In the upper part of the content box (about 25-55% of slide height), add four round-bulleted lines in black sans-serif, each with one bold blue (#0000CC) key phrase: (a) 'Compute the test point's distance from each training point' with 'Compute' bold blue; (b) 'Sort the distances in ascending (or descending) order' with 'Sort' bold blue; (c) 'Use the sorted distances to select the K nearest neighbors' with 'select the K nearest neighbors' bold blue; (d) 'Use majority rule (for classification) or averaging (for regression)' with 'majority rule' bold blue.
7. Leave a blank line, then start the note block (about 60-100% of slide height) with the plain line 'Note: K -Nearest Neighbors is called a non-parametric method' in black, with 'non-parametric' underlined.
8. Add a round bullet 'Unlike other supervised learning algorithms,' in black.
9. Add the emphasis line 'K -Nearest Neighbors doesn't:' in bold red (#CC0000) with 'doesn't' underlined.
10. Add two indented sub-bullets with en-dash markers in smaller black text: '– learn an explicit mapping f from the training data' and '– It simply uses the training data at the test time to make predictions'.
